newsitem.title: FINLAND: Wary Helsinki bourse falls in international trend.
newsitem.headline: Wary Helsinki bourse falls in international trend.

text.p: * Shares end clearly weaker but off early lows as Wall Street starts in jittery mood. Volume moderate weak as wary investors take wait-and- see approach. Forestries soft on weak pulp price outlook. HEX -1.75 pct at 2,394.76, adv-decl 18-69, unch 19
* Volume 342 million markka, 36 pct in Nokia
Finnish shares fell on Friday as Wall Street's jitters spread woes on European bourses and bond markets were nervously awaiting news about the planned budget stability pact, brokers said.
The forestry sector trimmed recent gains and fell sharply after pulp stocks were reported above expectations, making plans for price hikes seem less likely.
"This is due to the uncertainty over whether planned price rises will go through after the pulp inventories figures came in somewhat higher than expected," one broker said.
Pulp producer Metsa-Botnia said on friday it would refrain from a planned pulp price hike to $610 from $560.
Swedish forestry group Assidoman said the planned pulp price hikes were unlikely.
The forestry sub-index shed two percent with Metsa-Serla the biggest loser, down five percent or 1.60 markka at 31.70. UPM-Kymmene was liveliest, falling 1.50 markka to close at 92.70 markka.
Nokia ended the week 11 markka lower at 255.00 markka, down three percent for the day from Thursday's 263.00 close, on foreign selling, brokers said.
